course.description: Em menos de 90 minutos, você sai deste curso com uma tarefa real entregue por um agente de IA, e não apenas com uma explicação sobre como isso funciona. Em quatro oficinas e um Projeto Final, você abre o Codex dentro do ChatGPT, conecta um repositório de teste no GitHub, aprende a pedir uma tarefa do jeito certo e confere o trabalho do agente antes de aceitar. Não é preciso saber programar como profissional: basta topar clicar, testar e errar um pouco pelo caminho.

items.heading: Welcome to Hands-On AI Automation with Codex
items.paragraph: Welcome to your first step into practical AI automation! In this course, you won’t just read about how Codex and ChatGPT work—you’ll actually use them to complete a real task. We believe in learning by doing, so you’ll dive right in, experimenting and building your confidence as you go. By the end of this journey, you’ll have delivered a real result with the help of Codex, even if you’ve never used these tools before.

This lesson will guide you through the essential steps to get started with ChatGPT and Codex, including account setup, choosing the right tool for your needs, and preparing your workspace for automation.
Access ChatGPT and Codex interfaces to familiarize yourself with their features and capabilities.
Set up free accounts for both ChatGPT and GitHub to enable seamless integration and usage.
Learn how to decide when to ask Codex questions or delegate tasks, optimizing your workflow and productivity.
Prepare your workspace for automation by organizing your tools and environment for efficient task execution.

items.title: Introduction: Setting Up for Success
items.description: Before you can start automating tasks, you need to get your tools in place. This quick setup ensures you’re ready for hands-on practice.

items.title: Summary: Ready to Explore
items.description: With your accounts set up and Codex located, you’re ready to start exploring what these tools can do together.

items.title: Open ChatGPT in Your Browser
items.description: Launch your preferred web browser (like Chrome or Edge) and go to chatgpt.com.

items.title: Log In or Create a Free Account
items.description: If you already have a ChatGPT account, log in. If not, sign up for a free account—it only takes a few minutes.

items.title: Preview: Create a Free GitHub Account
items.description: While you won’t use GitHub just yet, you’ll need a free account for the next lesson. You can create one at github.com if you don’t have one already.

items.title: Find Codex in ChatGPT
items.description: Once logged in, look for Codex in the ChatGPT menu. Take note of the options available, such as modes for asking questions or generating code.

items.heading: Key Terms Flashcards
items.paragraph: Let’s clarify some key terms before you dive in. Review each flashcard to get comfortable with the language you’ll see throughout the course.

back.description: The main interface where you interact with AI, ask questions, and get responses in natural language.
An AI agent within ChatGPT designed to help automate tasks, generate code, and work on projects.
A specific instruction or request you give to ChatGPT or Codex to get a desired response or action.

items.heading: What’s the difference between asking Codex a question and delegating a task?
items.paragraph: Explore each section below to understand how Codex can either answer your questions or actually do the work for you. Knowing when to use each mode is key to getting the most out of your AI assistant.

items.title: When to use Ask Mode
items.description: Ask Mode is perfect for quick clarifications or explanations. In this mode, Codex will provide answers in text but won’t make any changes to your files or projects. Use it when you just need information or guidance.

items.title: When to use Task Mode
items.description: Task Mode allows Codex to perform real work, like editing files or generating code in a connected project. Choose this mode when you want Codex to take action and automate parts of your workflow.

items.title: Why it matters
items.description: Choosing the right mode ensures you get the results you want—whether that’s a simple answer or a completed task. Understanding this distinction will help you work more efficiently and avoid surprises.

items.title: If you want Codex to actually create or modify a file in your project, which mode should you use?

answers.title: Ask Mode
answers.feedback: Ask Mode is used for asking questions or getting explanations, not for performing actions like creating or modifying files.

answers.title: Task Mode
answers.feedback: Task Mode is the correct mode to use when you want Codex to perform real actions in your project, such as creating or modifying files.

answers.title: Chat Only
answers.feedback: Chat Only mode is for conversational interactions and does not allow Codex to perform actions in your project.

answers.title: None of the above
answers.feedback: There is a correct option listed: Task Mode. 'None of the above' is not correct.

items.paragraph: Remember: The first prompt rarely comes out perfect—and that’s okay! Adjusting your request is part of the process, not a mistake.

items.title: Practice Using Ask Mode
items.description: Let’s put your setup to the test by interacting with Codex in Ask Mode. This will help you see how Codex responds to questions without making any changes to your projects.

items.title: Understanding Ask Mode
items.description: You’ve now experienced how Ask Mode works—useful for getting information without making changes.

items.title: Select Codex and Ask Mode
items.description: In ChatGPT, select Codex from the menu and choose the “Ask” or equivalent mode.

items.title: Enter Your Question
items.description: Type exactly: O que é o Codex e em que tipo de tarefa eu deveria usá-lo?

items.title: Read the Response
items.description: Review the answer you receive. Notice that Codex provides an explanation but does not alter any files or projects.

items.title: Optional: Try Rephrasing
items.description: If you want more detail, try rephrasing your question to be more specific. For example, ask about programming or document organization tasks.

items.heading: Troubleshooting: What if something doesn’t work?
items.paragraph: Don’t worry if you hit a snag—everyone does at first! Expand each section below for quick solutions to common issues you might encounter.

items.title: Can’t find Codex in the menu?
items.description: Make sure you’re logged in to ChatGPT and look for “Codex” in the main menu. Availability may depend on your plan and region.

items.title: Response too generic?
items.description: If Codex gives you a vague answer, try asking your question again with more context. For example, specify if you’re asking about programming or document tasks.

items.title: General tips
items.description: For quick clarifications, stick with Ask Mode. It’s faster and safer when you don’t need to change anything in your project.

items.title: You ask Codex a question in Ask Mode and get a very generic answer. What should you do?

answers.title: Try again with more context
answers.feedback: This is correct. Providing more context helps Codex understand your question better and generate a more specific and useful response.

answers.title: Wait for a better answer
answers.feedback: Waiting will not change the answer you receive. You need to provide more information for a better response.

answers.title: Switch to Task Mode
answers.feedback: Switching to Task Mode is not necessary in this situation. Improving your question in Ask Mode is the best approach.

answers.title: Give up
answers.feedback: Giving up is not the best option. Try rephrasing your question with more details to get a better answer.

items.title: Continue
items.completeHint: Complete the content above before moving on.

items.paragraph: You’ve now accessed Codex and ChatGPT, practiced the basics, and are ready to set up your workspace for real task automation. In the next lesson, you’ll connect Codex to GitHub and delegate your first real task—putting your new skills to the test!

items.heading: Unlocking Real Automation: Connecting Codex to GitHub
items.paragraph: Integrating Codex with GitHub is the key to moving from simple Q&A to real, hands-on automation. By connecting these tools, you empower Codex to work directly on your projects—making changes, adding files, and delivering results you can see. This lesson will guide you through setting up this connection and show you how to delegate your first real task to an AI agent.
By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
Create and connect a GitHub repository for Codex
Authorize and manage Codex’s access to your repository
Formulate clear, effective prompts for AI agents
Delegate a real task to Codex

items.title: Setting Up Your Workspace
items.description: Before Codex can help with real tasks, it needs a place to work. You’ll set up a GitHub repository and connect it to Codex to create your own AI-powered workspace.

items.title: Ready for Automation
items.description: With your GitHub repository connected, you’ve set the stage for real automation. Next, you’ll learn how to craft effective prompts and delegate your first task.

items.title: Create a GitHub Account
items.description: If you don’t already have a GitHub account, go to github.com and sign up for a free account. This only takes a few minutes and is essential for the next steps.

items.title: Make a New Repository
items.description: Once logged in, create a new, empty repository. For practice, you might name it "meu-teste-codex". Leave it empty—no need to add files yet.

items.title: Connect Repository in Codex
items.description: In Codex, look for the option to connect or add a repository. Follow the prompts to start the connection process.

items.title: Authorize and Review Permissions
items.description: During the connection, you’ll be asked to authorize Codex to access your GitHub account. Review the permissions carefully before granting access.

items.title: Confirm Repository Connection
items.description: After authorization, check that your new repository appears within Codex. This means you’re ready to delegate tasks and see Codex in action!

items.heading: Troubleshooting Your GitHub Connection
items.paragraph: Explore each section below for solutions to common issues you might encounter while connecting Codex to GitHub. These tips will help you get back on track quickly and safely.

items.title: No option to connect GitHub?
items.description:
If you don’t see the option to connect GitHub in Codex, your ChatGPT session may have expired. Log out and log back in to refresh your session.

This simple step often resolves missing menu options or connection issues.

items.title: Repository not appearing?
items.description:
If your repository doesn’t show up in Codex after authorization, double-check your GitHub account settings. Make sure you’ve granted Codex access to the correct repository.

Sometimes, permissions need to be adjusted in your GitHub account or organization settings.

items.title: Safety First
items.description:
Always use a test repository for practice and review the permissions you grant to Codex. Avoid connecting important or sensitive projects until you’re comfortable with the process.

Being cautious with permissions protects your main work and ensures a safe learning environment.

items.paragraph: Tip: Always review what permissions you grant when connecting Codex to GitHub. For practice, use test repositories instead of important projects.

items.title: Continue
items.completeHint: Complete the content above before moving on.

items.heading: Key Elements of an Effective Task Prompt
items.paragraph: Review each flashcard to master the building blocks of a clear and actionable prompt for Codex. Knowing these elements will help you get better, more predictable results from your AI agent.

back.description: The specific task you want Codex to perform, such as adding a section to a file or fixing a bug.
Where the task should be done—like the file name, project, or area to focus on.
What Codex should avoid changing or touching during the task.
How you’ll know the task is complete—what outcome or result you expect to see.

items.paragraph:
When you give Codex a vague prompt, you leave a lot open to interpretation—often leading to unpredictable or incomplete results. By clearly stating the objective, context, restrictions, and success criteria, you help Codex understand exactly what you want and avoid unnecessary changes.

Well-structured prompts save time and reduce the need for corrections, making your workflow smoother and more reliable.

items.title: Start Your First Task with Codex
items.description: Now that your repository is connected, it’s time to delegate a real task to Codex. You’ll see firsthand how the quality of your prompt affects the outcome.

items.title: Compare Results
items.description: Notice the difference between the vague and well-structured prompts. Clear instructions lead to more accurate and predictable results from Codex.

items.title: Try a Vague Prompt
items.description: Open your connected repository in Codex and choose the option to generate or execute a task. Enter a vague prompt like: Melhora esse projeto. Observe how Codex responds and what changes, if any, are made.

items.title: Submit a Well-Structured Prompt
items.description: Start a new task and enter a detailed prompt: No arquivo README.md, adicione uma seção chamada 'Sobre o projeto' com uma frase explicando que este é um repositório de testes para aprender a usar o Codex. Não altere mais nada além disso. Critério de sucesso: o README passa a ter essa nova seção, sem perder o conteúdo que já existia.

items.title: Watch Codex Work
items.description: Follow the task’s progress in real time. Review the file changes and logs as Codex completes your request.

items.title: Which of the following best describes a well-structured prompt for Codex?

answers.title: Just say 'improve the project'
answers.feedback: This is too vague and does not provide enough detail for Codex to understand what needs to be improved or how.

answers.title: Specify what to do, where, what not to change, and how to know it's done
answers.feedback: This approach provides clear instructions, context, restrictions, and success criteria, which helps Codex deliver the desired results.

answers.title: Ask Codex to decide everything on its own
answers.feedback: Leaving all decisions to Codex can result in unpredictable or undesired outcomes due to lack of guidance.

answers.title: Only give the objective
answers.feedback: Providing only the objective lacks the necessary context and details for Codex to perform the task effectively.

items.heading: What if something goes wrong with your task?
items.paragraph: Explore these common issues and solutions to keep your workflow moving smoothly. Knowing how to troubleshoot will help you get the most out of Codex.

items.title: Task seems stuck?
items.description:
Some tasks, especially complex ones, can take longer to complete. Monitor the task log for updates and be patient if there’s no immediate progress.

Waiting a few extra minutes is normal for more involved requests.

items.title: Unexpected changes?
items.description:
If Codex changes more than you expected, your prompt may not have been specific enough about restrictions. Next time, clearly state what should not be altered.

Being precise helps prevent unwanted edits and saves time on corrections.

items.title: General prompt tips
items.description:
Always include the objective, context, restrictions, and success criteria in your requests. The clearer your instructions, the fewer errors or surprises you’ll encounter.

Good prompts make Codex more reliable and your workflow more efficient.

items.paragraph: Remember: A good request always includes objective, context, restrictions, and a clear success criterion. The clearer your instructions, the fewer corrections you’ll need later!

items.title: Continue
items.completeHint: Complete the content above before moving on.

items.paragraph: You’ve now connected Codex to your GitHub repository and successfully delegated your first real task. In the next lesson, you’ll learn how to review, approve, and deliver tasks completed by AI—ensuring every change meets your standards.

items.heading: Ensuring Quality: Reviewing and Delivering AI Tasks
items.paragraph: Before you accept any changes made by Codex, it’s essential to review the results with a critical eye. Even though Codex can automate tasks efficiently, skipping the review step can introduce errors or unwanted changes into your project. Just like in any professional environment, careful evaluation is the key to safe and effective automation. In this lesson, you’ll learn how to confidently review, approve, and deliver AI-completed tasks—ensuring every change meets your standards.
In this lesson, you will learn the essential steps involved in managing and completing a task effectively.
Monitor Task Outputs
Check Against Requirements
Approve or Revise Changes
Deliver a Completed Task

items.title: Continue
items.completeHint: Complete the content above before moving on.

items.title: Introduction to Reviewing a Codex Task
items.description: Begin by opening the completed task in Codex. This is where you’ll see the results of the AI’s work.

items.title: Summary of the Codex Task Review Process
items.description: By following these steps, you can effectively review and approve Codex tasks, ensuring that only the desired changes are made and that your project remains stable and accurate.

items.title: Review the Diff
items.description: Locate the diff (comparison) that shows exactly what has changed in your project files. Read through each line to confirm that only the requested changes were made.

items.title: Check the Task Log
items.description: Examine the task log for any errors or warnings that occurred during execution. This helps you spot issues that might not be obvious from the code alone.

items.title: Make a Decision
items.description: Decide whether to accept the result, request an adjustment, or ask Codex to try the task again. Only move forward if you fully understand and are satisfied with the changes.

items.title: Finalize the Task
items.description: If everything looks good, formally accept the change or open a Pull Request if you’re using GitHub. This completes the review and approval process.

items.heading: Key Concepts for Reviewing AI-Completed Tasks
items.paragraph: Review each flashcard to reinforce the essential concepts and tools you’ll use during the review process.

back.description: A diff shows the exact lines that were added, removed, or changed in your project files by Codex.
The task log records all actions, errors, and warnings during Codex’s execution—use it to spot problems.
Before accepting changes, check that the result matches your original request and meets all success criteria.

items.heading: Common Issues When Reviewing AI Tasks—and What to Do
items.paragraph: Explore each section to learn how to handle typical challenges you might face when reviewing Codex’s work. These tips will help you make safe, informed decisions.

items.title: Not sure why a line was changed?
items.description: If you’re unsure about a specific change, ask Codex directly for an explanation. Understanding every modification is crucial before approval.

items.title: Found an error in the log?
items.description: If the task log shows a failed test or error, do not accept the change. Instead, request a new execution and clearly explain what needs to be fixed.

items.title: General caution
items.description: Never accept changes you don’t fully understand. Human review is always essential, even if the output looks perfect at first glance.

items.title: You notice a change in your project that you didn’t expect. What should you do before accepting the task?

answers.title: Accept the change to save time
answers.feedback: Accepting changes without understanding them can lead to mistakes and issues later in the project.

answers.title: Ask Codex to explain the change and review the log
answers.feedback: Reviewing the log and asking for explanations ensures you understand the change and helps prevent mistakes.

answers.title: Ignore it and continue
answers.feedback: Ignoring unexpected changes can result in errors or unintended consequences in your project.

answers.title: Re-run the whole project
answers.feedback: Re-running the whole project is unnecessary before understanding the change and may waste time.

items.paragraph: Tip: Human review is never optional—even when the AI’s output looks perfect at first glance. Always double-check before you deliver!

items.title: Introduction: Practice a Real Task from Start to Finish
items.description: In this exercise, you will practice completing a real improvement task in your test repository, following the process from identifying an opportunity to delivering the final result.

items.title: Summary: Reflect on the Task Completion Process
items.description: By following these steps, you have practiced the full workflow of identifying, requesting, reviewing, and delivering a real improvement to your repository, reinforcing your understanding of the end-to-end process.

items.title: Choose an Improvement
items.description: Select a small, real improvement for your test repository. Examples include fixing a typo, updating the README file, or adding a helpful comment to the code.

items.title: Write Your Request
items.description: Draft a clear and structured prompt for the task. Be sure to include the objective, relevant context, and specific success criteria to define what a successful outcome looks like.

items.title: Submit and Monitor
items.description: Send your task to Codex and observe the execution process. Monitor the progress to ensure the task is being handled as expected.

items.title: Review Results
items.description: Carefully review the resulting diff and log. Check that the changes align with your expectations and meet the defined success criteria.

items.title: Approve or Open Pull Request
items.description: If you are satisfied with the changes, approve them or open a Pull Request to finalize and merge the improvement into your repository.

items.title: Summarize Your Work
items.description: Write a one-sentence summary describing what you delivered and why you accepted the result.

items.title: Continue
items.completeHint: Complete the content above before moving on.

items.paragraph: Careful review and human oversight are the foundation of safe, effective automation with Codex. You’ve now completed the full cycle: setting up your tools, delegating tasks, and delivering results you can trust. As you continue to practice, explore advanced features and more ambitious projects—your confidence and skills will only grow from here!
